verses.1:1: All wisdom comes from the Lord, and is with Him forever.
verses.1:2: The sand of the seas, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity—who shall number them?
verses.1:3: The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, the abyss, and wisdom—who shall trace them out?
verses.1:4: Before all things wisdom has been created, and the understanding of prudence is from everlasting.
verses.1:6: To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? And who has known her skillful designs?
verses.1:8: There is One who is wise, greatly to be feared, seated upon His throne.
verses.1:9: The Lord Himself created her, and saw and numbered her, and poured her out upon all His works,
verses.1:10: with all flesh according to His gift, and He bestowed her generously upon those who love Him.
verses.1:11: The fear of the Lord is glory and exultation, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing.
verses.1:12: The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart, and shall give gladness, and joy, and length of days.
verses.1:13: With him who fears the Lord it shall be well at the last, and in the day of his death he shall find favor.
verses.1:14: The beginning of wisdom is to fear God, and she was created together with the faithful in the womb.
verses.1:15: Among men she made an everlasting foundation her nest, and with their offspring she shall be trusted.
verses.1:16: The fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and she satiates them from her fruits.
verses.1:17: She shall fill all her house with desirable things, and the storehouses with her produce.
verses.1:18: The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, causing peace and the health of healing to flourish.
verses.1:19: He saw her and numbered her; He rained down skill and discerning knowledge, and exalted the glory of those who hold fast to her.
verses.1:20: The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are length of days.
verses.1:22: Unrighteous wrath cannot be justified; for the weight of his wrath is his downfall.
verses.1:23: A patient man will endure until the proper time, and afterward gladness shall spring up for him.
verses.1:24: Until the proper time he will conceal his words, and the lips of the faithful shall declare his understanding.
verses.1:25: In the treasuries of wisdom is a proverb of knowledge, but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
verses.1:26: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will generously bestow her upon you.
verses.1:27: For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction, and His good pleasure is faithfulness and meekness.
verses.1:28: Do not be disobedient to the fear of the Lord, and do not draw near to Him with a double heart.
verses.1:29: Do not be a hypocrite in the mouths of men, and keep watch over your lips.
verses.1:30: Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall and bring dishonor upon your soul; and the Lord will uncover your secrets and cast you down in the midst of the assembly, because you did not draw near in the fear of the Lord, and your heart was full of deceit.
verses.2:1: Child, if you come forward to serve the Lord God, prepare your soul for trial.
verses.2:2: Set your heart aright and be steadfast, and do not make haste in the time of calamity.
verses.2:3: Cling to Him and do not depart, so that you may be increased at your end.
verses.2:4: Accept whatever is brought upon you, and in the reversals of your humiliation be longsuffering.
verses.2:5: For gold is tested in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
verses.2:6: Trust in Him, and He will uphold you; make straight your ways, and hope in Him.
verses.2:7: You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy, and do not turn aside, lest you fall.
verses.2:8: You who fear the Lord, trust in Him, and your reward shall by no means fail.
verses.2:9: You who fear the Lord, hope for good things, and for everlasting gladness and mercy.
verses.2:10: Look to the generations of old and see: who ever trusted in the Lord and was put to shame? Or who remained steadfast in His fear and was forsaken? Or who called upon Him, and He disregarded him?
verses.2:11: For the Lord is compassionate and merciful, and forgives sins, and saves in the time of affliction.
verses.2:12: Woe to timid hearts and to slack hands, and to the sinner who walks upon two paths.
verses.2:13: Woe to a faint heart, for it does not trust; therefore it shall not be sheltered.
verses.2:14: Woe to you who have lost endurance! And what will you do when the Lord visits?
verses.2:15: Those who fear the Lord will not disobey His words, and those who love Him will keep His ways.
verses.2:16: Those who fear the Lord will seek His good pleasure, and those who love Him shall be filled with the law.
verses.2:17: Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and before Him they will humble their souls.
verses.2:18: Let us fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men; for as is His greatness, so also is His mercy.
verses.3:1: Hear me, your father, O children, and act accordingly, that you may be saved.
verses.3:2: For the Lord has honored a father over children, and has established the authority of a mother over sons.
verses.3:3: He who honors a father will make atonement for sins;
verses.3:4: and he who glorifies his mother is like one who stores up treasure.
verses.3:5: He who honors a father will be gladdened by children, and he who glorifies his mother is like one who stores up treasure; and in the day of his prayer he will be heard.
verses.3:6: He who glorifies a father will have long life, and he who obeys the Lord will give rest to his mother,
verses.3:7: and as to masters, he will serve those who brought him forth.
verses.3:8: In deed and in word honor your father, that a blessing may come upon you from him;
verses.3:9: for a father's blessing establishes the houses of children, but a mother's curse uproots foundations.
verses.3:10: Do not glory in the dishonor of your father, for there is no glory for you in dishonor;
verses.3:11: for a man's glory is from the honor of his father, and a mother in disgrace is a reproach to children.
verses.3:12: Child, care for your father in his old age, and do not grieve him during his lifetime;
verses.3:13: and even if he fails in understanding, have forbearance, and do not dishonor him in all your strength.
verses.3:14: For mercy toward a father will not be forgotten, and in place of sins it will be built up for you;
verses.3:15: in the day of your affliction you will be remembered; as fair weather upon frost, so your sins will melt away.
verses.3:16: He who forsakes a father is like a blasphemer, and he who provokes his mother to anger is cursed by the Lord.
verses.3:17: Child, perform your works in meekness, and you will be loved by an acceptable man;
verses.3:18: the greater you are, the more humble yourself, and before the Lord you will find favor;
verses.3:20: for great is the might of the Lord, and by the humble He is glorified.
verses.3:21: Do not seek things too hard for you, and do not examine things too strong for you.
verses.3:22: Reflect upon the things that have been commanded you, for you have no need of the hidden things.
verses.3:23: Do not meddle in matters beyond your works, for more than the understanding of men has been shown to you.
verses.3:24: For their own presumption has led many astray, and wicked conjecture has caused their minds to slip.
verses.3:26: And he who loves danger will fall into it; a stubborn heart will suffer evil at the last, a stubborn heart will be weighed down at the last.
verses.3:27: A stubborn heart will be weighed down with troubles, and the sinner will add sin upon sins.
verses.3:28: For the affliction of the proud there is no healing, for a plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
verses.3:29: The heart of a prudent man will ponder a parable, and a listening ear is the desire of a wise man.
verses.3:30: Water will quench a blazing fire, and almsgiving will make atonement for sins.
verses.3:31: He who repays favors is mindful of what comes afterward, and in the time of falling he will find support.
verses.4:1: Child, do not deprive the poor of his livelihood, and do not keep needy eyes waiting.
verses.4:2: Do not grieve a hungry soul, and do not provoke a man to anger in his distress.
verses.4:3: Do not add trouble to a heart provoked to anger, and do not delay a gift to one in need.
verses.4:4: Do not reject a suppliant in affliction, and do not turn your face away from a poor man.
verses.4:5: Do not turn your eye away from one in need, and do not give a man occasion to curse you;
verses.4:6: for when he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, He who made him will hear his supplication.
verses.4:7: Make yourself beloved to the assembly, and bow your head low before a great man.
verses.4:8: Incline your ear to the poor, and answer him with peaceful words in meekness.
verses.4:9: Deliver the wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer, and do not be fainthearted when you judge.
verses.4:10: Be like a father to orphans, and instead of a husband to their mother; and you will be like a son of the Most High, and He will love you more than your mother does.
verses.4:11: Wisdom has exalted her own sons, and she takes hold of those who seek her.
verses.4:12: He who loves her loves life, and those who rise early for her will be filled with gladness;
verses.4:13: he who holds fast to her will inherit glory, and wherever he enters, the Lord will bestow His blessing;
verses.4:14: those who serve her will minister to the Holy One, and those who love her the Lord loves;
verses.4:15: he who obeys her will judge nations, and he who draws near to her will dwell in confidence.
verses.4:16: If you trust, you will inherit her, and his generations will remain in possession;
verses.4:17: for at first she walks with him by crooked paths, and she will bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline until she trusts his soul, and she will test him with her ordinances;
verses.4:18: and again she will return straight to him and make him glad, and she will reveal to him her hidden things.
verses.4:19: If he goes astray, she will forsake him, and deliver him into the hands of his downfall.
verses.4:20: Observe the right time and guard yourself from evil, and concerning your soul do not be ashamed;
verses.4:21: for there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and grace.
verses.4:22: Do not show partiality against your own soul, and do not feel shame to your own downfall.
verses.4:23: Do not withhold speech in a time of salvation;
verses.4:24: for by speech wisdom will be known, and instruction by the word of the tongue.
verses.4:25: Do not speak against the truth, and be ashamed of your lack of instruction;
verses.4:26: do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not force the current of a river.
verses.4:27: And do not subject yourself to a foolish man, and do not show partiality to a ruler.
verses.4:28: Strive for the truth even to death, and the Lord God will fight for you.
verses.4:29: Do not be harsh in your tongue, and sluggish and slack in your works.
verses.4:30: Do not be like a lion in your house, and given to wild fancies among your household servants.
verses.4:31: Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive, and drawn back when it is time to repay.
verses.5:1: Do not rely on your riches, and do not say, "They are sufficient for me."
verses.5:2: Do not follow after your soul and your strength, to walk in the desires of your heart;
verses.5:3: and do not say, "Who shall have dominion over me?" For the Lord will surely execute vengeance upon you.
verses.5:4: Do not say, "I have sinned, and what has happened to me?" For the Lord is longsuffering.
verses.5:5: Concerning atonement, do not become fearless, to add sin upon sins;
verses.5:6: and do not say, "His compassion is great; He will atone for the multitude of my sins." For mercy and wrath are from Him, and His fury shall rest upon sinners.
verses.5:7: Do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day; for suddenly the wrath of the Lord shall go forth, and in the time of vengeance you shall perish.
verses.5:8: Do not rely on unrighteous riches; for you shall profit nothing in the day of calamity.
verses.5:9: Do not winnow in every wind, and do not walk in every path; so is the double-tongued sinner.
verses.5:10: Be steadfast in your understanding, and let your word be one.
verses.5:11: Be quick in your listening, and with patience utter an answer.
verses.5:12: If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be upon your mouth.
verses.5:13: Glory and dishonor are in speech, and the tongue of a man is his downfall.
verses.5:14: Do not be called a whisperer, and do not be ensnared by your tongue; for shame is upon the thief, and evil condemnation upon the double-tongued.
verses.5:15: In great matters and in small, do not act ignorantly, and instead of a friend do not become an enemy; for an evil name is shame, and it shall inherit reproach; so is the double-tongued sinner. Do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your soul, lest your soul be torn apart like a bull.
verses.6:3: You shall devour your leaves and destroy your fruits, and leave yourself like a dry tree.
verses.6:4: An evil soul will destroy the one who possesses it, and will make him a laughingstock to enemies.
verses.6:5: A sweet throat will multiply its friends, and a well-spoken tongue will multiply courteous greetings.
verses.6:6: Let those who are at peace with you be many, but your counselors one out of a thousand.
verses.6:7: If you acquire a friend, acquire him through testing, and do not quickly put your trust in him.
verses.6:8: For there is a friend for his own occasion, and he will by no means abide in the day of your affliction;
verses.6:9: and there is a friend who turns to enmity, and he will expose a quarrel to your reproach;
verses.6:10: and there is a friend who is a companion at tables, and he will by no means abide in the day of your affliction;
verses.6:11: and in your prosperity he will be like you, and over your household servants he will speak boldly;
verses.6:12: if you are brought low, he will be against you, and he will hide himself from your face.
verses.6:13: Separate yourself from your enemies, and beware of your friends.
verses.6:14: A faithful friend is a mighty shelter; and he who has found him has found a treasure.
verses.6:15: For a faithful friend there is no equivalent, and there is no weight to measure his excellence.
verses.6:16: A faithful friend is a medicine of life, and those who fear the Lord shall find him.
verses.6:17: He who fears the Lord directs his friendship aright, for as he is, so also is his neighbor.
verses.6:18: Child, from your youth choose instruction, and until gray hairs you shall find wisdom;
verses.6:19: like one who plows and one who sows, draw near to her, and wait for her good fruits; for in cultivating her you shall toil a little, and quickly you shall eat of her produce.
verses.6:20: How exceedingly swift she is to the uninstructed, and the senseless man will not abide in her;
verses.6:21: like a heavy stone of testing she shall be upon him, and he will not delay to cast her away.
verses.6:22: For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
verses.6:23: Listen, child, and receive my judgment, and do not refuse my counsel;
verses.6:24: and put your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her collar;
verses.6:25: put your shoulder under her and bear her, and do not be vexed at her bonds;
verses.6:26: with all your soul draw near to her, and with all your strength keep her ways.
verses.6:27: Search her out and seek her, and she shall be made known to you; and having taken hold of her, do not let her go;
verses.6:28: for at the last you shall find her rest, and she shall be turned for you into gladness;
verses.6:29: and the fetters shall be to you a shelter of strength, and her branches a robe of glory.
verses.6:30: For a golden ornament is upon her, and her bonds are a cord of blue;
verses.6:31: you shall put her on as a robe of glory, and you shall set upon yourself a crown of exultation.
verses.6:32: If you are willing, child, you shall be instructed, and if you apply your soul, you shall be prudent;
verses.6:33: if you love to listen, you shall receive it, and if you incline your ear, you shall be wise.
verses.6:34: Stand in the multitude of elders; and who is wise? Cling to him.
verses.6:35: Be willing to hear every godly discourse, and do not let proverbs of understanding escape you.
verses.6:36: If you see a man of understanding, rise early to go to him, and let your foot wear out the steps of his doors.
verses.6:37: Reflect upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in His commandments; He Himself shall establish your heart, and your desire for wisdom shall be given to you.
verses.7:1: Do not do evil deeds, and evil shall by no means overtake you.
verses.7:2: Depart from injustice, and it shall turn aside from you.
verses.7:3: Son, do not sow upon the furrows of unrighteousness, and you shall by no means reap them sevenfold.
verses.7:4: Do not seek authority from the Lord, nor a seat of honor from a king.
verses.7:5: Do not justify yourself before the Lord, and do not pretend to be wise before a king.
verses.7:6: Do not seek to become a judge, lest you lack the strength to remove injustices; lest you shrink in fear before the presence of a mighty man, and place a stumbling block in your uprightness.
verses.7:7: Do not sin against the multitude of a city, and do not cast yourself down in a crowd.
verses.7:8: Do not bind up sin a second time, for even in one you shall not be guiltless.
verses.7:9: Do not say, "He will look upon the multitude of my gifts, and when I bring an offering to God Most High, He will accept it."
verses.7:10: Do not be fainthearted in your prayer, and do not neglect to give alms.
verses.7:11: Do not mock a man who is in the bitterness of his soul, for there is One who humbles and exalts.
verses.7:12: Do not plow falsehood against your brother, nor do the same to a friend.
verses.7:13: Do not desire to utter any falsehood, for its continual practice is not for good.
verses.7:14: Do not prattle in the assembly of elders, and do not repeat a word in your prayer.
verses.7:15: Do not hate toilsome labor and farming, which was created by the Most High.
verses.7:16: Do not reckon yourself among the multitude of sinners.
verses.7:17: Humble your soul exceedingly. Remember that wrath will not delay, for the vengeance upon the ungodly is fire and the worm.
verses.7:18: Do not exchange a friend for the sake of money, nor a true brother for the gold of Souphir.
verses.7:19: Do not forgo a wise and good wife, for her grace is above gold.
verses.7:20: Do not mistreat a servant who labors in truth, nor a hired laborer who gives his soul.
verses.7:21: Let your soul love a good servant; do not deprive him of freedom.
verses.7:22: Do you have livestock? Look after them, and if they are useful to you, let them remain with you.
verses.7:23: Do you have children? Discipline them, and bend their neck from youth.
verses.7:24: Do you have daughters? Watch over their body, and do not make your countenance cheerful toward them.
verses.7:25: Give a daughter in marriage, and you will have accomplished a great work; and bestow her upon a man of understanding.
verses.7:26: Do you have a wife dear to your soul? Do not cast her out.
verses.7:27: With all your heart honor your father, and do not forget the birth pangs of your mother.
verses.7:28: Remember that through them you were born, and what will you repay them as they have done for you?
verses.7:29: With all your soul revere the Lord, and hold His priests in honor.
verses.7:30: With all your strength love Him who made you, and do not forsake His ministers.
verses.7:31: Fear the Lord and honor the priest, and give him his portion as you have been commanded from the beginning: the offering for trespass, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits.
verses.7:32: Extend your hand also to the poor, that your blessing may be made complete.
verses.7:33: Let the grace of a gift be before every living person, and do not withhold grace from the dead.
verses.7:34: Do not hold back from those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
verses.7:35: Do not hesitate to visit a sick person, for by such deeds you shall be loved.
verses.7:36: In all your words remember your final end, and you shall never sin.
verses.8:1: Do not contend with a mighty man, lest you fall into his hands.
verses.8:2: Do not quarrel with a rich man, lest he outweigh you in the balance; for gold has destroyed many, and has turned aside the hearts of kings.
verses.8:3: Do not contend with a loud-tongued man, and do not pile wood upon his fire.
verses.8:4: Do not jest with an undisciplined man, lest your forefathers be dishonored.
verses.8:5: Do not reproach a man who turns away from sin; remember that we are all under penalty.
verses.8:6: Do not dishonor a man in his old age, for some of us also are growing old.
verses.8:7: Do not rejoice over a dead man; remember that we all die.
verses.8:8: Do not neglect the discourse of the wise, and occupy yourself with their proverbs; for from them you shall learn instruction, and how to serve great men.
verses.8:9: Do not pass over the discourse of the aged, for they themselves learned from their fathers; for from them you shall learn understanding, and how to give an answer in the time of need.
verses.8:10: Do not kindle the coals of a sinner, lest you be burned in the fire of his flame.
verses.8:11: Do not rise up in the presence of an insolent man, lest he lie in wait as an ambush for your mouth.
verses.8:12: Do not lend to a man stronger than yourself; and if you lend, count yourself as one who has lost it.
verses.8:13: Do not become surety beyond your means; and if you become surety, take thought as one who must pay.
verses.8:14: Do not go to law against a judge, for according to his honor they will judge in his favor.
verses.8:15: Do not travel on the road with a reckless man, lest he become a heavy burden upon you; for he will act according to his own will, and by his folly you shall perish along with him.
verses.8:16: Do not enter into strife with a wrathful man, and do not travel with him through the wilderness; for blood is as nothing in his eyes, and where there is no help he will strike you down.
verses.8:17: Do not take counsel with a fool, for he will not be able to keep a word secret.
verses.8:18: Before a stranger do not do a secret thing, for you do not know what he will bring forth.
verses.8:19: Do not reveal your heart to every man, and do not let him return you a favor.
verses.9:1: Do not be jealous of the wife of your bosom, nor teach an evil lesson against yourself.
verses.9:2: Do not give your soul to a woman, that she should tread upon your strength.
verses.9:3: Do not go to meet a loose woman, lest you fall into her snares.
verses.9:4: Do not keep constant company with a woman who plays music, lest you be captured by her schemes.
verses.9:5: Do not gaze intently upon a virgin, lest you stumble into the penalties for her.
verses.9:6: Do not give your soul to harlots, lest you lose your inheritance.
verses.9:7: Do not look around in the streets of a city, nor wander about in its deserted places.
verses.9:8: Turn your eye away from a comely woman, and do not gaze intently upon beauty that belongs to another; by the beauty of a woman many have been led astray, and from this, love is kindled like fire.
verses.9:9: Do not sit at all with a married woman, nor revel with her in wine, lest your soul incline toward her, and in your spirit you slip into destruction.
verses.9:10: Do not forsake an old friend, for the new one is not equal to him; new wine is a new friend: when it has grown old, you shall drink it with gladness.
verses.9:11: Do not envy the glory of a sinner, for you do not know what his overthrow will be.
verses.9:12: Do not delight in the delight of the ungodly; remember that even until Hades they shall by no means be justified.
verses.9:13: Keep far away from a man who has authority to slay, and you shall by no means entertain the fear of death; and even if you approach him, do not offend, lest he take away your life. Know well that you pass through the midst of snares, and you walk upon the battlements of cities.
verses.9:14: According to your strength, take the measure of your neighbors, and take counsel with the wise.
verses.9:15: And let your discourse be with those of understanding, and all your conversation be in the law of the Most High.
verses.9:16: Let righteous men be your table companions, and let your glorying be in the fear of the Lord.
verses.9:17: By the hand of craftsmen a work shall be praised, and the ruler of a people is wise in his speech.
verses.9:18: A loose-tongued man is dreaded in his city, and he who is rash in his speech shall be hated.
verses.10:1: A wise judge will instruct his people, and the rule of one who has understanding shall be well-ordered.
verses.10:2: As is the judge of his people, so also are his ministers; and as is the ruler of the city, so are all who dwell in it.
verses.10:3: An undisciplined king will destroy his people, and a city shall be built up through the understanding of its rulers.
verses.10:4: In the hand of the Lord is the authority of the earth, and He will raise up the right one over it at the appointed time.
verses.10:5: In the hand of the Lord is the prosperity of a man, and upon the face of the scribe He will set His glory.
verses.10:6: Do not harbor anger against your neighbor for every wrong, and do nothing in deeds of arrogance.
verses.10:7: Pride is hateful before the Lord and men, and against both it will commit unjust deeds.
verses.10:8: A kingdom is transferred from nation to nation because of injustices, insolence, and wealth.
verses.10:9: Why are earth and ashes proud? Because even in life I have cast away his inward parts.
verses.10:10: The physician mocks a lingering illness; he is king today, and tomorrow he shall die.
verses.10:11: For when a man dies, he shall inherit creeping things and beasts, even worms.
verses.10:12: The beginning of pride is a man departing from the Lord, and his heart has turned away from Him who made him.
verses.10:13: For the beginning of pride is sin, and he who holds fast to it shall pour forth abomination. Therefore the Lord made their calamities extraordinary, and overthrew them utterly.
verses.10:14: The Lord cast down the thrones of rulers, and seated the meek in their place.
verses.10:15: The Lord plucked up the roots of nations, and planted the humble in their place.
verses.10:16: The Lord overthrew the lands of nations, and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
verses.10:17: He withered some of them and destroyed them, and caused their remembrance to cease from the earth.
verses.10:18: Pride was not created for men, nor fierce wrath for those born of women.
verses.10:19: What offspring is honorable? The offspring of man. What offspring is honorable? Those who fear the Lord. What offspring is dishonorable? The offspring of man. What offspring is dishonorable? Those who transgress commandments.
verses.10:20: In the midst of brethren their leader is honorable, and those who fear the Lord are honorable in His eyes.
verses.10:22: The rich, the noble, and the poor—their glorying is the fear of the Lord.
verses.10:23: It is not right to dishonor a poor man of understanding, nor is it fitting to honor a sinful man.
verses.10:24: The nobleman, the judge, and the ruler shall be honored, yet not one of them is greater than he who fears the Lord.
verses.10:25: Free men shall serve a wise servant, and a man of knowledge will not murmur.
verses.10:26: Do not make a show of wisdom in doing your work, and do not glorify yourself in the time of your distress.
verses.10:27: Better is he who works in all things than he who strolls about, or he who glorifies himself and lacks bread.
verses.10:28: Child, in meekness glorify your soul, and give it honor according to its worth.
verses.10:29: Who will justify him who sins against his own soul? And who will honor him who dishonors his own life?
verses.10:30: A poor man is honored because of his knowledge, and a rich man is honored because of his wealth.
verses.10:31: And he who is honored in poverty—how much more in wealth? And he who is without honor in wealth—how much more in poverty?
verses.11:1: The wisdom of the humble lifts up his head, and shall seat him in the midst of great men.
verses.11:2: Do not praise a man for his beauty, and do not abhor a man for his appearance.
verses.11:3: Small among flying creatures is the bee, yet the chief of sweet things is her fruit.
verses.11:4: Do not boast in the wearing of garments, and in the day of glory do not exalt yourself; for wondrous are the works of the Lord, and hidden are His works among men.
verses.11:5: Many rulers have sat upon the ground, while one never thought of has worn a diadem.
verses.11:6: Many mighty men have been exceedingly dishonored, and men of renown have been delivered into the hands of companions.
verses.11:7: Before you examine, do not find fault; consider first, and then rebuke.
verses.11:8: Do not answer before you have heard, and in the midst of words do not interrupt.
verses.11:9: Do not contend concerning a matter that does not concern you, and in the judgment of sinners do not sit in council.
verses.11:10: Child, do not let your undertakings be about many things; if you multiply them, you shall not be held guiltless; and if you pursue, you shall by no means overtake, nor shall you escape by fleeing.
verses.11:11: There is one who labors and toils and hastens, and is all the more in want.
verses.11:12: There is one who is sluggish and in need of help, lacking in strength and abounding in poverty; yet the eyes of the Lord looked upon him for good, and He raised him up from his low estate,
verses.11:13: and He lifted up his head, and many marveled at him.
verses.11:14: Good things and evil, life and death, poverty and riches are from the Lord.
verses.11:17: The gift of the Lord abides with the godly, and His good pleasure shall prosper forever.
verses.11:18: There is one who grows rich through his carefulness and stinginess, and this is the portion of his reward:
verses.11:19: When he says, "I have found rest, and now I will eat of my good things," he does not know what time will pass, and he shall leave them to others and die.
verses.11:20: Stand firm in your covenant and attend to it, and grow old in your work.
verses.11:21: Do not marvel at the works of a sinner; trust in the Lord and abide in your toil; for it is an easy thing in the eyes of the Lord swiftly and suddenly to make a poor man rich.
verses.11:22: The blessing of the Lord is in the reward of the godly, and in a swift hour He causes His blessing to flourish.
verses.11:23: Do not say, "What is my need, and what good things shall be mine from now on?"
verses.11:24: Do not say, "I have enough, and what harm shall I suffer from now on?"
verses.11:25: In the day of prosperity there is forgetfulness of adversity, and in the day of adversity prosperity will not be remembered;
verses.11:26: for it is an easy thing before the Lord in the day of death to repay a man according to his ways.
verses.11:27: The affliction of an hour causes forgetfulness of delight, and at the end of a man is the revelation of his works.
verses.11:28: Before his death do not call anyone blessed, and by his children a man shall be known.
verses.11:29: Do not bring every man into your house, for many are the snares of the deceitful.
verses.11:30: A decoy partridge in a basket—so is the heart of the proud, and like a spy he watches for a downfall.
verses.11:31: For turning good things into evil he lies in wait, and upon admirable things he will lay blame.
verses.11:32: From a spark of fire a heap of burning coals is multiplied, and a sinful man lies in wait for blood.
verses.11:33: Beware of an evildoer, for he contrives wicked things, lest he bring upon you a blemish forever.
verses.11:34: Lodge a stranger in your house, and he will overturn you with troubles and estrange you from your own.
verses.12:1: If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there shall be gratitude for your good deeds.
verses.12:2: Do good to a godly man, and you shall find repayment, and if not from him, yet from the Most High.
verses.12:3: No good belongs to the one who persists in evil, nor to the one who does not bestow alms.
verses.12:4: Give to the godly man, and do not assist the sinner.
verses.12:5: Do good to the humble, and do not give to the ungodly; withhold his bread and do not give to him, lest through it he overpower you; for you shall find double evil for all the good that you do for him.
verses.12:6: For the Most High also hates sinners, and will repay vengeance upon the ungodly.
verses.12:7: Give to the good man, and do not assist the sinner.
verses.12:8: A friend will not be vindicated in prosperity, and an enemy will not be hidden in adversity.
verses.12:9: In a man's prosperity his enemies are in grief, and in his adversity even his friend will withdraw.
verses.12:10: Never trust your enemy; for as bronze corrodes, so does his wickedness.
verses.12:11: Even if he humbles himself and walks bowed down, keep your soul alert and guard yourself from him; and you shall be toward him like one who has wiped clean a mirror, and you shall know that it has not completely corroded.
verses.12:12: Do not set him beside yourself, lest having overthrown you, he stand in your place; do not seat him at your right hand, lest he seek your seat, and at the last you shall recognize my words and be pierced with remorse at my sayings.
verses.12:13: Who will pity a charmer bitten by a serpent, and all who draw near to wild beasts?
verses.12:14: So it is with one who draws near to a sinful man and becomes entangled in his sins.
verses.12:15: For an hour he will remain with you, yet if you turn aside, he will by no means stand firm.
verses.12:16: With his lips the enemy will speak sweetly, yet in his heart he will plot to overthrow you into a pit; with his eyes the enemy will weep, yet if he finds an opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.
verses.12:17: If calamities meet you, you shall find him there before you, and as though helping, he will trip up your heel;
verses.12:18: he will shake his head and clap his hands, and whisper many things, and change his countenance.
verses.13:1: He who touches pitch shall be defiled, and he who keeps company with a proud man shall become like him.
verses.13:2: Do not lift a burden beyond you, and do not keep company with one stronger and wealthier than yourself. What fellowship shall an earthen pot have with a cauldron? The pot will strike against it, and it will be shattered.
verses.13:3: A rich man has done wrong, and moreover he fumes with indignation; a poor man has been wronged, and moreover he must plead.
verses.13:4: If you are useful, he will make use of you; and if you come to want, he will forsake you.
verses.13:5: If you have possessions, he will live with you and empty you out, and he himself will not be troubled.
verses.13:6: He has need of you, and he will lead you astray; he will smile upon you and give you hope; he will speak fair words to you and say, "What is your need?"
verses.13:7: And he will put you to shame with his feasts until he has emptied you out twice or three times, and in the end he will mock you; afterward he will see you and forsake you, and he will shake his head over you.
verses.13:8: Take heed lest you be led astray, and do not be brought low in your gladness.
verses.13:9: When a mighty man summons you, hold yourself back, and so much the more he will summon you.
verses.13:10: Do not press forward, lest you be thrust away, and do not stand far off, lest you be forgotten.
verses.13:11: Do not presume to speak as an equal with him, and do not trust his many words; for with much talk he will test you, and as though smiling upon you he will examine you.
verses.13:12: Merciless is he who does not guard words, and he will by no means spare you from affliction and chains.
verses.13:13: Guard yourself and take great heed, for you walk alongside your own downfall.
verses.13:15: Every living creature loves its own kind, and every man his neighbor.
verses.13:16: All flesh gathers together according to its kind, and a man will cling to one like himself.
verses.13:17: What fellowship shall a wolf have with a lamb? So is a sinner with a godly man.
verses.13:18: What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? And what peace is there between a rich man and a poor man?
verses.13:19: Wild donkeys in the wilderness are the prey of lions; so the poor are the pasture of the rich.
verses.13:20: Humility is an abomination to the proud; so is a poor man an abomination to the rich.
verses.13:21: When a rich man totters, he is steadied by friends; but when a humble man falls, he is thrust further away by friends.
verses.13:22: When a rich man slips, there are many helpers; he speaks things that ought not to be spoken, and they justify him. A humble man slips, and they moreover rebuke him; he utters understanding, and no place is given to him.
verses.13:23: A rich man speaks, and all keep silence, and they exalt his word to the clouds; a poor man speaks, and they say, "Who is this?" And if he stumbles, they will overthrow him besides.
verses.13:24: Wealth is good in which there is no sin, and poverty is evil in the mouth of a godly man.
verses.13:25: The heart of a man alters his countenance, whether for good or for evil.
verses.13:26: The mark of a heart in good fortune is a cheerful countenance, and the finding of proverbs is thought with toil.
verses.14:1: Blessed is the man who has not slipped with his mouth, and has not been pierced with sorrow for sin.
verses.14:2: Blessed is he whose own soul does not condemn him, and who has not fallen from his hope.
verses.14:3: Wealth is not fitting for a stingy man, and of what use are riches to an envious man?
verses.14:4: He who gathers by denying his own soul gathers for others, and others will revel in his good things.
verses.14:5: He who is wicked to himself, to whom will he be good? And he shall by no means rejoice in his riches.
verses.14:6: There is no one worse than he who begrudges himself, and this is the repayment of his own wickedness.
verses.14:7: Even if he does good, he does it by oversight, and in the end he reveals his wickedness.
verses.14:8: Wicked is the man who grudges with his eye, turning away his face and despising souls.
verses.14:9: The eye of a covetous man is not satisfied with a portion, and wicked injustice shall dry up the soul.
verses.14:10: An evil eye is grudging over bread, and goes wanting at his own table.
verses.14:11: Child, according to what you have, do good to yourself, and bring worthy offerings to the Lord.
verses.14:12: Remember that death will not delay, and the covenant of Hades has not been shown to you.
verses.14:13: Before you die, do good to a friend, and according to your ability reach out and give to him.
verses.14:14: Do not deprive yourself of a good day, and let no share of a worthy desire pass you by.
verses.14:15: Will you not leave your toils to another, and your labors to be divided by lot?
verses.14:16: Give and receive, and indulge your soul, for in Hades there is no seeking of luxury.
verses.14:17: All flesh grows old like a garment; for the covenant from of old is, "You shall surely die."
verses.14:18: Like flourishing foliage on a leafy tree—some it casts down, and others it brings forth—so is a generation of flesh and blood: one dies, and another is born.
verses.14:19: Every decaying work passes away, and he who fashions it shall depart with it.
verses.14:20: Blessed is the man who shall die in wisdom, and who shall reason in his understanding.
verses.14:21: He who ponders her ways in his heart shall also gain insight into her hidden things.
verses.14:22: Go forth after her like a tracker, and lie in wait at her entryways.
verses.14:23: He who peers through her windows will also listen at her doorways.
verses.14:24: He who lodges close by her house will also drive a tent peg into her walls.
verses.14:25: He shall pitch his tent right beside her, and he shall lodge in a lodging place of good things.
verses.14:26: He shall place his children in her shelter, and under her branches he shall abide.
verses.14:27: He shall be sheltered by her from the scorching heat, and in her glory he shall dwell.
verses.15:1: He who fears the Lord will do this, and he who holds fast to the law shall obtain her.
verses.15:2: And she shall come to meet him like a mother, and like a virgin bride she shall welcome him.
verses.15:3: She shall feed him with the bread of understanding, and give him the water of wisdom to drink.
verses.15:4: He shall lean upon her and shall not be swayed, and he shall hold fast to her and shall not be put to shame.
verses.15:5: And she shall exalt him above his neighbors, and in the midst of the assembly she shall open his mouth.
verses.15:6: He shall inherit gladness and a crown of rejoicing and an everlasting name.
verses.15:7: Men without understanding shall by no means lay hold of her, and sinful men shall not see her.
verses.15:8: She is far from pride, and lying men shall never remember her.
verses.15:9: Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent from the Lord.
verses.15:10: For praise shall be spoken in wisdom, and the Lord will make it prosper.
verses.15:11: Do not say, "Because of the Lord I fell away"; for what He hates, you shall not do.
verses.15:12: Do not say, "He Himself led me astray"; for He has no need of a sinful man.
verses.15:13: The Lord hates every abomination, and it is not beloved by those who fear Him.
verses.15:14: He Himself from the beginning made man, and left him in the hand of his own counsel.
verses.15:15: If you choose, you shall keep the commandments, and to practice faithfulness is a matter of good will.
verses.15:16: He has set fire and water before you; to whichever you desire, you shall stretch out your hand.
verses.15:17: Before men are life and death, and whichever one chooses shall be given to him.
verses.15:18: For great is the wisdom of the Lord; He is mighty in power and beholds all things.
verses.15:19: And His eyes are upon those who fear Him, and He Himself shall know every work of man.
verses.15:20: And He has commanded no one to act ungodly, and He has given no one license to sin.
verses.16:1: Do not desire a multitude of unprofitable children, nor rejoice over ungodly sons.
verses.16:2: Though they multiply, do not rejoice over them; if the fear of the Lord is not with them,
verses.16:3: do not trust in their life, and do not rely upon their place; for one is better than a thousand, and to die childless than to have ungodly children.
verses.16:4: For by one man of understanding a city shall be populated, but a tribe of lawless ones shall be made desolate.
verses.16:5: Many such things I have seen with my eyes, and mightier things than these my ear has heard.
verses.16:6: In an assembly of sinners a fire shall be kindled, and in a disobedient nation wrath was kindled.
verses.16:7: He did not pardon the giants of old, who rebelled in their strength;
verses.16:8: He did not spare those among whom Lot sojourned, whom He abhorred because of their arrogance;
verses.16:9: He did not have mercy on the nation of destruction, those who were swept away in their sins,
verses.16:10: and likewise six hundred thousand foot soldiers, those who were gathered together in their hardness of heart.
verses.16:11: Even if there is one stiff-necked man, it is a wonder if he shall go unpunished; for mercy and wrath are with Him—mighty in forgiveness, and pouring out wrath.
verses.16:12: According to His great mercy, so also is His great reproof; He will judge a man according to his works.
verses.16:13: A sinner shall not escape with his plunder, and He will by no means delay the endurance of the godly.
verses.16:14: He will make a place for every act of mercy; each one shall find according to his works.
verses.16:17: Do not say, "I shall be hidden from the Lord, and who from on high will remember me? Among so great a people I shall by no means be remembered, for what is my soul in a measureless creation?"
verses.16:18: Behold, heaven and the heaven of the heaven of God, the deep and the earth, shall be shaken at His visitation.
verses.16:19: Together the mountains and the foundations of the earth quake with trembling when He looks upon them.
verses.16:20: And upon these things no heart will ponder; and who will consider His ways?
verses.16:21: And a tempest, which no man shall see—and the greater part of His works are in hidden places.
verses.16:22: Who will declare the works of righteousness, or who will wait for them? For the covenant is far off.
verses.16:23: One who is lacking in heart ponders these things, and a foolish and erring man ponders foolish things.
verses.16:24: Hear me, child, and learn knowledge, and attend to my words with your heart.
verses.16:25: I bring forth instruction by weight, and with exactness I declare knowledge.
verses.16:26: In the judgment of the Lord were His works from the beginning, and from their making He divided their portions.
verses.16:27: He set His works in order forever, and their dominions throughout their generations; they neither hungered nor grew weary, and they did not cease from their works.
verses.16:28: Not one pressed upon his neighbor, and forever they shall not disobey His word.
verses.16:29: And after these things the Lord looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things.
verses.16:30: With the life of every living creature He covered its face, and to it is their return.
verses.17:1: The Lord created man out of the earth, and turned him back to it again.
verses.17:2: He gave them numbered days and an appointed time, and He gave them authority over the things upon it.
verses.17:3: Befitting themselves He clothed them with strength, and according to His own image He made them.
verses.17:4: And He placed the fear of him upon all flesh, so that he should have dominion over wild beasts and birds.
verses.17:6: Discretion, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart to think He gave to them.
verses.17:7: He filled them with knowledge of understanding, and showed them good and evil.
verses.17:8: He set His eye upon their hearts, to show them the majesty of His works,
verses.17:10: that they might declare the mighty deeds of His works. And they shall praise the name of holiness.
verses.17:11: He added knowledge to them, and bequeathed to them a law of life.
verses.17:12: He established an everlasting covenant with them, and showed them His judgments.
verses.17:13: Their eyes beheld the majesty of glory, and their ear heard the glory of their voice.
verses.17:14: And He said to them, "Beware of all unrighteousness," and He commanded each one of them concerning his neighbor.
verses.17:15: Their ways are continually before Him; they shall not be hidden from His eyes.
verses.17:17: Over every nation He appointed a ruler, and Israel is the Lord's portion.
verses.17:19: All their works are like the sun before Him, and His eyes are continually upon their ways.
verses.17:20: Their iniquities have not been hidden from Him, and all their sins are before the Lord.
verses.17:22: A man's act of mercy is like a signet with Him, and He will preserve a man's kindness as the apple of the eye.
verses.17:23: Afterward He will rise up and repay them, and He will return their recompense upon their own head.
verses.17:24: Yet to those who repent He granted a return, and He comforted those whose endurance was failing.
verses.17:25: Turn to the Lord and forsake sins; make supplication before His face, and lessen offense.
verses.17:26: Return to the Most High and turn away from iniquity, and intensely hate abomination.
verses.17:27: Who will praise the Most High in Hades, instead of the living and those who render thanksgiving?
verses.17:28: From the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving perishes; he who is alive and whole shall praise the Lord.
verses.17:29: How great is the mercy of the Lord, and forgiveness to those who turn to Him!
verses.17:30: For all things cannot be in men, because a son of man is not immortal.
verses.17:31: What is brighter than the sun? Yet this too fails; and an evil man will ponder flesh and blood.
verses.17:32: He Himself inspects the host of the height of heaven, and all men are earth and ashes.
verses.18:1: He who lives forever created all things together.
verses.18:2: The Lord alone shall be justified.
verses.18:4: To no one has He granted to declare His works, and who shall trace out His mighty deeds?
verses.18:5: Who shall reckon the might of His majesty? And who shall proceed to recount His mercies?
verses.18:6: It is not possible to diminish nor to add, and it is not possible to trace out the wondrous works of the Lord.
verses.18:7: When a man has finished, then he begins, and when he ceases, then he shall be perplexed.
verses.18:8: What is man, and what is his usefulness? What is his good, and what is his evil?
verses.18:9: The number of a man's days is at most one hundred years.
verses.18:10: As a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand, so are a few years in a day of eternity.
verses.18:11: Therefore the Lord was longsuffering toward them, and poured out His mercy upon them.
verses.18:12: He saw and perceived their downfall, that it is evil; therefore He multiplied His forgiveness.
verses.18:13: The mercy of man is upon his neighbor, but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh—reproving and chastening and teaching, and bringing back as a shepherd his flock.
verses.18:14: He has mercy on those who receive discipline, and on those who hasten after His judgments.
verses.18:15: Child, in good deeds do not give reproach, nor in any gift grief of words.
verses.18:16: Will not dew relieve the scorching heat? So is a word better than a gift.
verses.18:17: Behold, is not a word better than a good gift? And both are with a gracious man.
verses.18:18: A fool will ungraciously reproach, and the gift of a grudging man wastes away the eyes.
verses.18:19: Before you speak, learn, and before sickness, seek treatment.
verses.18:20: Before judgment examine yourself, and in the hour of visitation you shall find forgiveness.
verses.18:21: Before you fall sick, humble yourself, and in the time of sins, show repentance.
verses.18:22: Do not be hindered from paying a vow in due time, and do not wait until death to be justified.
verses.18:23: Before making a vow, prepare yourself, and do not become like a man who tests the Lord.
verses.18:24: Remember wrath in the days of the end, and the time of vengeance in the turning away of the face.
verses.18:25: Remember the time of famine in the time of abundance, poverty and want in the days of wealth.
verses.18:26: From morning until evening the time changes, and all things are swift before the Lord.
verses.18:27: A wise man shall be cautious in everything, and in days of sins he shall guard himself from trespass.
verses.18:28: Every man of understanding knows wisdom, and to him who finds her he shall give praise.
verses.18:29: Those who have understanding in words have themselves also become wise, and have poured forth accurate proverbs.
verses.18:30: Self-control of the soul. Do not go after your desires, and restrain yourself from your appetites.
verses.18:31: If you grant your soul the satisfaction of desire, it will make you a laughingstock to your enemies.
verses.18:32: Do not delight in great luxury; do not be bound to its expense.
verses.18:33: Do not become poor by carousing on borrowed money, when you have nothing in your purse.
verses.19:1: A drunken workman shall not become rich; he who despises small things shall fall little by little.
verses.19:2: Wine and women will turn men of understanding astray, and he who clings to harlots shall become more reckless.
verses.19:3: Decay and worms shall inherit him, and a reckless soul shall be cut off.
verses.19:4: He who trusts quickly is light of heart, and he who sins shall offend against his own soul.
verses.19:5: He who rejoices in heart shall be condemned.
verses.19:6: And he who hates babbling has less of evil.
verses.19:7: Never repeat a word, and you shall suffer no loss at all.
verses.19:8: Whether to friend or to enemy, do not recount it; and unless it is a sin for you, do not reveal it.
verses.19:9: For he has heard you and has guarded himself against you, and in due time he shall hate you.
verses.19:10: Have you heard a word? Let it die with you. Take courage—it shall by no means burst you.
verses.19:11: Because of a word a fool shall be in travail, as a woman giving birth because of an infant.
verses.19:12: An arrow stuck fast in a thigh of flesh—so is a word in the belly of a fool.
verses.19:13: Confront a friend—perhaps he did not do it; and if he did anything, that he may not do it again.
verses.19:14: Confront your friend—perhaps he did not say it; and if he has said it, that he may not repeat it.
verses.19:15: Confront a friend, for often there is slander, and do not believe every word.
verses.19:16: There is one who slips, and not from his soul; and who has not sinned with his tongue?
verses.19:17: Confront your neighbor before threatening him, and give place to the law of the Most High.
verses.19:20: All wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom is the doing of the law.
verses.19:22: And the knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, nor is the counsel of sinners anywhere prudence.
verses.19:23: There is wickedness, and it is an abomination; and there is a fool who is lacking in wisdom.
verses.19:24: Better is one who is inferior in understanding yet filled with fear, than one who abounds in prudence and transgresses the law.
verses.19:25: There is a meticulous craftiness, and it is unjust; and there is one who perverts favor to bring forth a judgment.
verses.19:26: There is one who does evil, bowed down in gloom, yet his inward parts are full of deceit.
verses.19:27: Bowing down his face and feigning deafness, where he has not been recognized he will overtake you.
verses.19:28: And if through lack of strength he is hindered from sinning, if he finds an opportunity, he will do evil.
verses.19:29: By his appearance a man shall be known, and by the meeting of his countenance a discerning man shall be known.
verses.19:30: The attire of a man, and the laughter of his teeth, and a man's steps declare what concerns him.
verses.20:1: There is a reproof that is not timely, and there is one who keeps silent, and he is prudent.
verses.20:2: How much better it is to reprove than to be angry,
verses.20:3: and he who confesses shall be kept back from loss.
verses.20:4: Like the lust of a eunuch to deflower a maiden, so is he who executes judgments by violence.
verses.20:5: There is one who keeps silent and is found wise, and there is one who is hated for much speaking.
verses.20:6: There is one who keeps silent, for he has no answer; and there is one who keeps silent, knowing the proper time.
verses.20:7: A wise man will keep silent until the proper time, but the braggart and the fool will overstep the time.
verses.20:8: He who multiplies words shall be abhorred, and he who takes authority upon himself shall be hated.
verses.20:9: There is success for a man amid misfortunes, and there is a windfall that turns to loss.
verses.20:10: There is a gift that will not profit you, and there is a gift whose recompense is twofold.
verses.20:11: There is loss on account of glory, and there is one who from lowliness has lifted up his head.
verses.20:12: There is one who buys much for little, yet pays for it sevenfold.
verses.20:13: The wise man will make himself beloved by his speech, but the favors of fools shall be poured out.
verses.20:14: The gift of a fool will not profit you, for his eyes are many in place of one.
verses.20:15: He will give little and reproach much, and he will open his mouth like a herald; today he will lend, and tomorrow he will demand it back—such a man is hateful.
verses.20:16: A fool will say, "I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good deeds; those who eat my bread are wicked of tongue."
verses.20:17: How often, and how many, will laugh him to scorn?
verses.20:18: A slip on the pavement is better than a slip of the tongue; so shall the downfall of the wicked come swiftly.
verses.20:19: An ungracious man is an untimely tale; it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
verses.20:20: A proverb from the mouth of a fool shall be rejected, for he will not speak it in its season.
verses.20:21: There is one who is kept from sinning by want, and in his rest he shall not be pierced with remorse.
verses.20:22: There is one who destroys his own soul through shame, and because of a foolish person he will destroy it.
verses.20:23: There is one who out of shame makes a promise to a friend, and he gains him as an enemy for nothing.
verses.20:24: A lie is a foul blemish in a man; it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
verses.20:25: A thief is preferable to one who continually lies, yet both shall inherit destruction.
verses.20:26: The character of a lying man is dishonor, and his shame is with him continually.
verses.20:27: Words of proverbs. The wise man will advance himself by words, and a prudent man will please great men.
verses.20:28: He who tills the ground shall raise high his heap of grain, and he who pleases great men shall atone for wrongdoing.
verses.20:29: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and like a muzzle in the mouth, they turn aside reproofs.
verses.20:30: Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure—what profit is there in either of them?
verses.20:31: Better is a man who conceals his folly than a man who conceals his wisdom.
verses.21:1: Child, have you sinned? Do not do so any more, and pray concerning your former sins.
verses.21:2: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if you draw near, it will bite you; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
verses.21:3: All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; for its wound there is no healing.
verses.21:4: Terror and arrogance will lay waste riches; thus the house of the proud shall be laid waste.
verses.21:5: The prayer of a poor man goes from his mouth to His ears, and His judgment comes swiftly.
verses.21:6: He who hates reproof is in the track of a sinner, but he who fears the Lord will repent in his heart.
verses.21:7: He who is mighty in tongue is known from afar, but the discerning man knows whenever he slips.
verses.21:8: He who builds his house with the money of others is like one who gathers his stones for winter.
verses.21:9: The assembly of the lawless is tow gathered together, and their end is a flame of fire.
verses.21:10: The way of sinners is paved smooth with stones, yet at its end is the pit of Hades.
verses.21:11: He who keeps the law masters his thoughts, and the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.
verses.21:12: He who is not shrewd will not be instructed; yet there is a shrewdness that multiplies bitterness.
verses.21:13: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood, and his counsel is like a fountain of life.
verses.21:14: The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will retain no knowledge at all.
verses.21:15: If a man of understanding hears a wise word, he will praise it and add to it; the self-indulgent man hears it and it displeases him, and he casts it behind his back.
verses.21:16: The discourse of a fool is like a burden on a journey, but grace shall be found upon the lip of the discerning.
verses.21:17: The mouth of a prudent man shall be sought in the assembly, and they will ponder his words in their heart.
verses.21:18: Like a house laid in ruins, so is wisdom to a fool, and the knowledge of the senseless is unexamined words.
verses.21:19: Instruction is fetters on the feet of the foolish, and like shackles upon the right hand.
verses.21:20: A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a shrewd man will scarcely smile quietly.
verses.21:21: Like a golden ornament is instruction to a prudent man, and like a bracelet upon the right arm.
verses.21:22: The foot of a fool is swift to enter a house, but a man of much experience will show modesty before another's presence.
verses.21:23: A fool peers from the doorway into a house, but a well-instructed man will stand outside.
verses.21:24: It is lack of discipline in a man to listen at the door, and the prudent man shall be weighed down with disgrace.
verses.21:25: The lips of strangers shall be weighed down with these things, but the words of the prudent shall be weighed in a balance.
verses.21:26: In the mouth of fools is their heart, but the heart of the wise is their mouth.
verses.21:27: When an ungodly man curses Satan, he curses his own soul.
verses.21:28: A whisperer defiles his own soul, and he shall be hated in his neighborhood.
verses.22:1: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and everyone will hiss at his disgrace.
verses.22:2: A slothful man is compared to a lump of dung from a dunghill; everyone who picks it up will shake off his hand.
verses.22:3: A father's shame is in the birth of an undisciplined son, and a daughter is born to his loss.
verses.22:4: A prudent daughter will obtain a husband for herself, but she who brings shame is a grief to the one who fathered her.
verses.22:5: A shameless woman brings shame upon both father and husband, and she will be dishonored by both.
verses.22:6: Like music in mourning is an untimely tale, but scourges and discipline belong to wisdom at every season.
verses.22:9: He who teaches a fool is gluing together a potsherd, and rousing a sleeper from a deep sleep.
verses.22:10: He who tells a tale to a fool tells it to one who is drowsy, and at the conclusion he will say, "What is it?"
verses.22:11: Weep over the dead, for light has failed him; and weep over a fool, for understanding has failed him. Weep more gently over the dead, for he has found rest; but the life of the fool is worse than death.
verses.22:12: Mourning for the dead is seven days, but for a fool and an ungodly man it is all the days of his life.
verses.22:13: Do not multiply words with a fool, and do not go to one who lacks understanding. Guard yourself against him, lest you suffer trouble, and you shall not be defiled by his spattering; turn aside from him and you shall find rest, and you shall not be wearied by his senselessness.
verses.22:14: What is heavier than lead? And what is its name other than a fool?
verses.22:15: Sand and salt and a mass of iron are easier to bear than a man without understanding.
verses.22:16: Timber bracing bound into a building will not be loosened in an earthquake; so a heart established upon considered counsel will not grow fearful when the time comes.
verses.22:17: A heart settled upon thoughtful understanding is like stucco ornament upon a polished wall.
verses.22:18: Stakes set upon a high place will not stand firm against the wind; so a fearful heart set upon a foolish thought will not stand firm against any terror.
verses.22:19: He who pricks an eye brings forth tears, and he who pricks a heart reveals its feeling.
verses.22:20: He who casts a stone at birds drives them away, and he who reproaches a friend will dissolve friendship.
verses.22:21: If you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way of return.
verses.22:22: If you open your mouth against a friend, do not be afraid, for there is reconciliation—except for reproach, and arrogance, and the revealing of a secret, and a treacherous blow; from these things every friend will flee away.
verses.22:23: Gain the trust of your neighbor in his poverty, that you may be filled together with him in his prosperity; remain steadfast with him in a time of affliction, that you may share with him in his inheritance.
verses.22:24: Before fire come the vapor of a furnace and smoke; so before bloodshed come revilings.
verses.22:25: I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, and I will not hide myself from his presence;
verses.22:26: and if evil things befall me on his account, everyone who hears of it will beware of him.
verses.22:27: Who will set a guard over my mouth, and a prudent seal upon my lips, that I may not fall through it, and that my tongue may not destroy me?
verses.23:1: O Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not forsake me to their counsel, and do not let me fall because of them.
verses.23:2: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they may not spare my errors, and that it may not pass over their sins,
verses.23:3: so that my errors may not multiply and my sins may not abound, lest I fall before my adversaries and my enemy rejoice over me?
verses.23:4: O Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me haughtiness of eyes,
verses.23:5: and turn lust away from me.
verses.23:6: Do not let appetite of the belly and fleshly passion overtake me, and do not give me over to a shameless soul.
verses.23:7: Discipline of the mouth. Hear the discipline of the mouth, children, and he who keeps it shall by no means be caught; by his own lips
verses.23:8: the sinner and the reviler and the arrogant shall be caught; they shall stumble by them.
verses.23:9: Do not accustom your mouth to an oath, and do not make a habit of naming the Holy One.
verses.23:10: For just as a servant who is continually examined under punishment will not be free from bruises, so also he who swears and continually names Him shall by no means be cleansed from sin.
verses.23:11: A man of many oaths shall be filled with lawlessness, and the scourge shall not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin is upon him; and if he disregards it, he has sinned doubly; and if he has sworn in vain, he shall not be acquitted, for his house shall be filled with calamities.
verses.23:12: There is a manner of speech clothed about with death; may it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob, for all these things shall be far from the godly, and they shall not wallow in sins.
verses.23:13: Do not accustom your mouth to foul coarseness, for in it there is a word of sin.
verses.23:14: Remember your father and your mother, for among great men one sits in council; lest you forget yourself before them and by your habit act the fool, and wish that you had not been born, and lest you curse the day of your birth.
verses.23:15: A man accustomed to words of reproach shall by no means be disciplined in all his days.
verses.23:17: Two kinds multiply sins, and the third shall bring on wrath. A passionate soul is like a burning fire; it shall by no means be quenched until it is consumed. A fornicator in the body of his flesh shall by no means cease until he kindles a fire. To a fornicator all bread is sweet; he shall by no means desist until he dies.
verses.23:18: A man who transgresses from his own bed, saying in his soul, "Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls conceal me, and no one sees me; why should I be afraid? The Most High will by no means remember my sins."
verses.23:19: And the eyes of men are his fear, and he does not know that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, looking upon all the ways of men and perceiving into hidden places.
verses.23:20: Before all things were created, they were known to Him; and so also after they were brought to completion.
verses.23:21: This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he did not expect it, he shall be seized.
verses.23:22: So also is a woman who forsakes her husband and brings forth an heir by another man.
verses.23:23: For first, she has disobeyed the law of the Most High; and second, she has trespassed against her own husband; and third, she has committed adultery in fornication, and has brought forth children by another man.
verses.23:24: She shall be brought out before the assembly, and there shall be a visitation upon her children.
verses.23:25: Her children shall not strike root, and her branches shall not yield fruit.
verses.23:26: She shall leave behind her memory for a curse, and her reproach shall not be blotted out.
verses.23:27: And those who remain shall know that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing is sweeter than to give heed to the commandments of the Lord.
verses.24:1: The praise of Wisdom. Wisdom shall praise her own soul, and in the midst of her people she shall glory.
verses.24:2: In the assembly of the Most High she shall open her mouth, and before His host she shall glory:
verses.24:3: "I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and like a mist I covered the earth.
verses.24:4: I dwelt in the high places, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
verses.24:5: Alone I encompassed the circuit of heaven, and in the depth of the abysses I walked.
verses.24:6: In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I gained a possession.
verses.24:7: Among all these I sought a resting place, and in whose inheritance shall I abide?
verses.24:8: Then the Creator of all things commanded me, and He who created me caused my tent to rest and said, 'Make your dwelling in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel.'
verses.24:9: Before eternity, from the beginning, He created me, and to eternity I shall never cease.
verses.24:10: In the holy tabernacle I ministered before Him, and so in Zion I was established.
verses.24:11: In the beloved city likewise He gave me rest, and in Jerusalem was my authority.
verses.24:12: And I took root among a glorified people, in the portion of the Lord, His inheritance.
verses.24:13: Like a cedar I grew tall in Lebanon, and like a cypress on the mountains of Hermon.
verses.24:14: Like a palm tree I grew tall on the shores, and like rose plants in Jericho; like a fair olive tree in the plain, and I grew tall like a plane tree.
verses.24:15: Like cinnamon and aromatic aspalathus I gave forth a scent, and like choice myrrh I spread abroad a sweet aroma, like galbanum, and onycha, and stacte, and like the vapor of frankincense in the tabernacle.
verses.24:16: Like a terebinth I stretched out my branches, and my branches are branches of glory and grace.
verses.24:17: I am like a vine putting forth grace, and my blossoms are the fruit of glory and riches.
verses.24:19: Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled with my produce.
verses.24:20: For the remembrance of me is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance is sweeter than the honeycomb.
verses.24:21: Those who eat me shall still hunger, and those who drink me shall still thirst.
verses.24:22: He who obeys me shall not be put to shame, and those who labor in me shall not sin."
verses.24:23: All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law that Moses commanded as an inheritance for the congregations of Jacob.
verses.24:25: It overflows with wisdom like the Pishon, and like the Tigris in the days of new fruits;
verses.24:26: it fills up understanding like the Euphrates, and like the Jordan in the days of harvest;
verses.24:27: it makes instruction shine forth like light, like the Gihon in the days of vintage.
verses.24:28: The first man did not finish knowing her, and likewise the last has not searched her out.
verses.24:29: For her thought is fuller than the sea, and her counsel deeper than the great abyss.
verses.24:30: And I, like a canal from a river, and like a water conduit, went forth into an orchard.
verses.24:31: I said, "I will water my garden, and I will drench my flower bed." And behold, my canal became a river, and my river became a sea.
verses.24:32: I will yet make instruction shine like the dawn, and I will reveal these things far away.
verses.24:33: I will yet pour out teaching like prophecy, and I will leave it for generations forever.
verses.24:34: See that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who diligently seek it.
verses.25:1: In three things I was adorned, and I stood forth beautiful before the Lord and men: the harmony of brethren, and the friendship of neighbors, and a wife and husband who walk together in agreement.
verses.25:2: And three kinds my soul hates, and I greatly loathe their way of life: a proud poor man, and a rich liar, an old adulterer lacking in understanding.
verses.25:3: In youth you have not gathered, and how could you find in your old age?
verses.25:4: How comely is judgment for gray hairs, and for elders to know counsel!
verses.25:5: How comely is the wisdom of the aged, and understanding and counsel for those held in honor!
verses.25:6: The crown of the aged is rich experience, and their glory is the fear of the Lord.
verses.25:7: Nine thoughts I have called blessed in my heart, and the tenth I will speak with my tongue: a man who rejoices over his children, living and looking upon the downfall of enemies;
verses.25:8: blessed is he who dwells with a wife of understanding, and he who has not slipped with his tongue, and he who has not served one unworthy of himself;
verses.25:9: blessed is he who has found prudence, and he who speaks to the ears of those who listen;
verses.25:10: how great is he who has found wisdom! Yet there is none above him who fears the Lord.
verses.25:11: The fear of the Lord surpasses everything; he who holds fast to it, to whom shall he be likened?
verses.25:13: Any wound, but not a wound of the heart; and any wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman;
verses.25:14: any affliction, but not affliction from those who hate; and any vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies.
verses.25:15: There is no head above the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
verses.25:16: I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon than live in a house with a wicked woman.
verses.25:17: The wickedness of a woman alters her appearance, and darkens her countenance like sackcloth.
verses.25:18: In the midst of his neighbors her husband shall recline at table, and upon hearing, he groans bitterly.
verses.25:19: Small is every malice compared to the malice of a woman; may the lot of a sinner fall upon her!
verses.25:20: Like a sandy ascent to the feet of an old man, so is a talkative wife to a quiet husband.
verses.25:21: Do not fall before the beauty of a woman, and do not long after a woman.
verses.25:22: There is wrath and shamelessness and great shame if a wife supports her husband.
verses.25:23: A dejected heart, a gloomy countenance, and a wound of the heart—this is a wicked wife; drooping hands and feeble knees—she who does not make her husband happy.
verses.25:24: From a woman was the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die.
verses.25:25: Do not give water an outlet, nor authority to a wicked woman.
verses.25:26: If she does not walk according to your hand, cut her off from your own flesh.
verses.26:1: Blessed is the husband of a good wife, and the number of his days is twofold.
verses.26:2: A virtuous wife gladdens her husband, and he shall fulfill his years in peace.
verses.26:3: A good wife is a good portion; she shall be given in the portion of those who fear the Lord.
verses.26:4: Whether rich or poor, his heart is glad, and at every season his countenance is cheerful.
verses.26:5: Of three things my heart has been fearful, and before a fourth countenance I have made supplication: the slander of a city, and the assembly of a mob, and a false accusation—all these are more grievous than death.
verses.26:6: Grief of heart and mourning is a wife jealous of another wife, and a scourge of the tongue that makes it known to all.
verses.26:7: A shaking ox-yoke is a wicked wife; he who takes hold of her is like one who grasps a scorpion.
verses.26:8: Great wrath is a drunken wife, and she will not conceal her shame.
verses.26:9: A woman's harlotry is in the lifting up of her eyes, and by her eyelids it shall be known.
verses.26:10: Over a daughter strengthen the watch unswervingly, lest, finding liberty, she make use of it for herself.
verses.26:11: Keep watch behind a shameless eye, and do not marvel if she transgresses against you.
verses.26:12: As a thirsty traveler opens his mouth and drinks from any water near at hand, she will sit down before every stake, and before an arrow she will open her quiver.
verses.26:13: A wife's grace shall delight her husband, and her understanding shall fatten his bones.
verses.26:14: A gift of the Lord is a silent wife, and there is no exchange for a disciplined soul.
verses.26:15: Grace upon grace is a modest wife, and no weight is worthy of a self-controlled soul.
verses.26:16: Like the sun rising in the heights of the Lord, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of his house.
verses.26:17: Like a lamp shining forth upon a holy lampstand, so is the beauty of a face upon a stately stature.
verses.26:18: Like golden pillars upon a silver base, so are beautiful feet upon the breast of a steadfast woman.
verses.26:28: At two things my heart has been grieved, and at a third wrath has come upon me: a warrior suffering want through poverty, and men of understanding if they are held in contempt, and one who turns back from righteousness to sin—the Lord shall prepare him for the sword.
verses.26:29: Scarcely shall a merchant keep himself free from wrongdoing, and a tradesman shall not be acquitted of sin.
verses.27:1: For the sake of a trifle many have sinned, and he who seeks to increase will turn away his eye.
verses.27:2: Between the joints of stones a peg shall be driven fast, and between selling and buying sin shall be squeezed in.
verses.27:3: If he does not hold fast diligently in the fear of the Lord, swiftly his house shall be overthrown.
verses.27:4: In the shaking of a sieve the refuse remains; so does a man's filth in his reasoning.
verses.27:5: The furnace tests the potter's vessels, and the testing of a man is in his discourse.
verses.27:6: The fruit of a tree reveals its cultivation; so does speech reveal the thought of a man's heart.
verses.27:7: Before discourse, do not praise a man, for this is the testing of men.
verses.27:8: If you pursue righteousness, you shall attain it, and you shall put it on like a robe of glory.
verses.27:9: Birds will lodge with their own kind, and truth will return to those who practice it.
verses.27:10: A lion lies in wait for prey; so do sins for those who practice unrighteousness.
verses.27:11: The discourse of a godly man is always wisdom, but the fool changes like the moon.
verses.27:12: In the midst of those without understanding watch the time, but in the midst of a thoughtful man remain continually.
verses.27:13: The discourse of fools is an offense, and their laughter is in the wantonness of sin.
verses.27:14: The talk of one who swears many oaths makes the hair stand on end, and their strife is a stopping of the ears.
verses.27:15: The strife of the proud is a shedding of blood, and their reviling is grievous to hear.
verses.27:16: He who reveals secrets has destroyed trust, and he shall never find a friend after his own soul.
verses.27:17: Love a friend and keep faith with him; but if you reveal his secrets, you shall not pursue after him.
verses.27:18: For as a man has destroyed his enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbor.
verses.27:19: And as you have let a bird go from your hand, so you have let your neighbor go, and you shall not catch him.
verses.27:20: Do not pursue him, for he has gone far away, and has escaped like a gazelle from a snare.
